unit.why: A first-person memorate: as a nine-year-old at the Seer of Lublin's Pesach seder, the narrator saw fire on the Seer's head and was given the zeroa as a form of semikhah.
unit.boundary_note: Section header 'מענין סמיכה' sits at the end of the previous division; the trailing header 'מענין ספר תורה' belongs to the next division.

stories.start_quote: ואצל רבינו מו״ר מוה׳ יעקב יצחק מלובלין
stories.summary_en: The narrator recalls visiting the Seer of Lublin as a child with his father on Pesach; he saw fire and light on the Seer's head, and on the second seder night the Seer, after three tries, gave him the zeroa, a gesture of semikhah in the Besht's power that later sustained him against his persecutors.
